children: Basis bids for soybeans shipped by barge to US Gulf Coast export terminals were flat to lower on Wednesday on rising futures prices and quiet demand, traders said.
Corn barge basis bids were also steady to lower on light demand.
Steep corn and soybean futures rallies on Tuesday following bullish supply forecasts from the US Department of Agriculture chilled exporter buying interest and weighed on basis values.

Exporters are awaiting further large US soybean purchases by China as the country works toward its 25-million-metric-ton annual buying commitment. Traders estimate that Chinese government buyers have booked around 18 million to 19 million tons to date.

Private importers have relied on South American soy instead due to costly tariffs on US shipments. Many have already filled their immediate needs and are now looking to new-crop Brazilian shipments for shipment in the first quarter of 2027, traders said.
The USDA is due to release weekly export sales data on Friday, a day later than usual due to a US federal holiday this week.

CIF soybean barges loaded in November traded at 103 cents a bushel over Chicago Board of Trade January futures (SF27) and were re-bid at 102 cents over futures, down from bids of 104 cents over futures a day earlier. December barges traded at 112 cents over futures before bids slipped to 110 cents over late in the day, steady with bids late on Tuesday.
FOB basis offers for soybeans loaded in December were 118 cents over futures and January loadings were offered at 120 cents over futures, both down a penny from a day earlier.

CIF corn barges loaded in November were bid at 94 cents over CBOT December (CZ26) futures, steady with trades on Tuesday. December-loaded barges were bid 99 cents over futures, down 2 cents from trades a day earlier.
FOB export premiums for Gulf corn vessels loaded in December dipped by a penny to 108 cents over futures.
